Definition: from G1537 and G5015; to disturb wholly:--exceedingly trouble.
BiblicalUsage: ektarássō is the word for exceedingly trouble. In Acts 16:20, the text says "do exceedingly trouble our city."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, ektarássō means exceedingly trouble, nothing more and nothing less.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison
